subject: MSA redline: indemnity backstop + evidence custody (Astra Health)
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan@astrahealth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: LegalOps <legal@astrahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on indemnity backstop + evidence custody (MSA redline)

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Our legal team reviewed Redwood's latest MSA redline and have two high-level asks before procurement can move to signature: 1) a clear "indemnity backstop" definition for third‑party IP claims (we need to understand what triggers Redwood's obligation vs. our insurer), and 2) where evidence will be hosted if a takedown/claim occurs (we prefer vendor‑hosted custody for chain-of-custody continuity).

I've attached Astra_Routed_Evidence_List.xlsx with examples of the types of artifacts we expect to collect. Can Redwood confirm whether you can host a read‑only evidence bundle for the duration of an investigation and accept a liability backstop limited to direct damages capped at the order form amount?

We'd like to get this resolved this week if possible — procurement deadline is Friday.

Best,
Jordan
Legal & Procurement, Astra Health

Attachments: Astra_Routed_Evidence_List.xlsx

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>

Cc: LegalOps <legal@astrahealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on indemnity backstop + evidence custody (MSA redline)

Jordan — thanks for the clarity and the attachment. 

Quick answers up front: we can host an evidence bundle in a secure read‑only S3 bucket for investigations and provide access logs/audit trails; for the indemnity backstop we typically offer defense and indemnity for third‑party IP claims with a cap linked to the order form value or a negotiated multiple.

Routing this to Karthik and our legal lead Laura to propose precise language that satisfies Astra's procurement team while preserving Redwood's enterprise risk parameters.

Action items:
- Karthik/Laura: propose a redline clause and a short operations SLA for evidence custody (see attachments in my next note).
- Jordan: can you confirm your preferred order form cap (order amount or 2x/3x) and whether Astra requires access to raw KV cache snapshots if relevant?

I can escalate to Dev if there are technical questions about snapshotting.

Thanks — Aisha
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Jordan Ellis <jordan@astrahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on indemnity backstop + evidence custody (MSA redline)

Jordan/Aisha — looping in Laura (legal) and Dev (ops). High‑level proposals from Redwood legal/ops side:

1) Indemnity backstop wording (draft): "Redwood will defend and indemnify Customer against third‑party claims alleging infringement of third‑party intellectual property arising from the unmodified Model outputs provided pursuant to the Order Form, subject to Customer's prompt notice and cooperation. The aggregate liability for indemnity shall not exceed the total fees paid by Customer under the applicable Order Form in the 12 months prior to the claim."

2) Evidence custody (ops): Redwood can provision a restricted, read‑only evidence bundle stored in a customer‑scoped S3 bucket for the duration of active investigations (default retention 90 days unless extended by mutual agreement). Access will be logged; we can provide a certified export package on request. If Astra requires retention longer than 90 days, we'll need a written SOW for storage and preservation costs.

3) Operational caveats: we cannot provide KV cache snapshots that contain other customers' context; we can provide per‑request logs and the generated content payloads associated with the claim. Dev — can you confirm retention/exports and estimated lead time for a custodial snapshot?

If Astra is comfortable with an Order Form cap equal to the 12‑month fees, we can proceed with this redline. If Astra needs a higher ceiling (2x), Laura — please advise on legal acceptability.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Sales Operations

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan@astrahealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on indemnity backstop + evidence custody (MSA redline)

Jordan — thanks, and appreciate the FYI on procurement timing. Two legal clarifications and a suggested compromise: 

1) Cap mechanics: Redwood accepts an aggregate indemnity cap tied to the greater of (i) total fees paid under the applicable Order Form in the prior 12 months or (ii) a mutually agreed fixed dollar amount. We would resist open‑ended multiples (e.g., unlimited 3x) without insurance offsets.

2) Evidence custody: we will host a read‑only evidence bundle as Karthik described. We will not host or export any datasets that include other customers' inputs; exports will be scoped to Astra's requests. For preservation beyond 90 days, we propose a short SOW covering storage and retention costs and a signature from Astra.

3) Proposed redline language (short): "For third‑party claims of infringement attributable to Redwood's model outputs, Redwood's aggregate indemnity liability shall be limited to the fees paid by Customer under the applicable Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim. Redwood will provide a read‑only evidence bundle and audit logs on request to support claim review; preservation beyond 90 days requires an executed statement of work covering costs."

If Astra confirms the 12‑month cap or proposes a fixed dollar alternative, we can circulate a v3 redline (PDF) today.

- Laura
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Astra_MSA_redline_v3.pdf
